name: c3bot-relay
description: c3bot-relay (#1579): Telegram <-> c3 relay. Ingestion: the c3-bot (Bot A) in webhook mode via the public c3-pub route /c3bot-webhook (secret_token checked), fallback Bot B getUpdates only while the webhook is unhealthy, deduped by chat+message_id+date. Inbound events fan out to c3 clients over three transports: WebSocket (/ws, full duplex), Server-Sent Events (/events, Last-Event-ID resume) and long-poll (/poll, cursor). Outbound via POST /send or a WS send frame, sent as Bot A. Zero npm dependencies. API bearer-gated, mesh-only; only the webhook path is public.

primary._auth_doc: auth none: the app gates every call itself with its own bearer (C3BOT_RELAY_TOKEN, 401 without it; /health is open). The fleet forward_auth would reject this token and buffer SSE; the route stays WG-only. streaming:true keeps SSE and WebSocket unbuffered.

api.description: Telegram <-> c3 relay: WS /ws, SSE /events, long-poll /poll, POST /send.

secrets._doc: Values only in the private vault at Linux-Containers/infra-ops_c3bot-relay/src/ (sops, public fleet recipient; the Ship overlay copies secrets.yaml and its secrets.*.yaml fragments in, the engine merges them and mounts .secrets as env_file). Four keys by NAME. C3BOT_RELAY_TOKEN: 64-hex bearer of the relay API (CI sops-create generates it; cloud-infra-mcp reads the same value through a consumer fragment); the server exits 78 when empty. C3BOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET: 64-hex Telegram secret_token of the Bot A webhook (CI sops-create, secrets.webhook.yaml); the webhook route answers 503 without it and 401 on a wrong header. C3BOT_A_BOT_TOKEN: the token of the existing c3-bot (Bot A, the same token cloud-infra-mcp holds as C3_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN), copied by CI into secrets.bot-a.yaml; used for setWebhook/getWebhookInfo and for outbound sendMessage. C3BOT_RELAY_BOT_TOKEN: the token of the DEDICATED fallback Bot B (minted in @BotFather by the owner, added to the group with privacy mode OFF); it polls getUpdates only while the webhook path is unhealthy. Webhook and getUpdates never share a token, so there is no 409. While Bot B's token is absent the relay runs webhook-only and /health reports ingest.fallback 'degraded: Bot B token missing'.
